response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner default-entry structure, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong local-exit targets by contrasting exact source-inventory obligations with the closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) the root/system->Operate initial-entry contract is satisfied by OffState->OperateState via 'start' and OperateState's own [*]->IdleRegion default entry, but each of the three regions inside OperateState (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) is itself a composite that owns a required default entry into its sole named operating leaf state (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState respectively per NL1/NL3 containment contracts), and none of those three regions has an initial edge targeting its named leaf state; each region's only initial pseudostate edge targets a synthetic 'UnspecifiedInitial' placeholder instead. This is a structural default-entry defect distinct from the already-satisfied outer Operate entry, so I derive three owner-scoped initial_entry contracts. (2) The AccelerateRegion's initial edge to CruisingState (transition:line:25) is conditional (guard R45RouteToken==6, no trigger), which the deterministic facts and verify_facts explicitly flag as INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted for initial-entry semantics; it cannot satisfy the region's default-entry obligation to AcceleratingState/CruisingState. (3) NL1-GROUP-DECL and NL3-GROUP-1 (Idle<->Accelerating/Cruising/Braking substate transitions) are represented in source only via region-to-region edges (IdleRegion->AccelerateRegion, etc.), never via edges naming the leaf states Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking directly; since those leaf states are unreachable from initial (per inspection/verify facts), the group-level transition endpoints are effectively wrong_target/unreachable relative to the named substates. (4) NL3-DERIVED event-consumer-coverage for 'stopping' is structurally consistent (Stop event has reachable consumers), so omitted. (5) The NL1-DERIVED guard_disjointness (Idle->Accelerating vs Idle->Braking) is not contrastively supported since IdleRegion->AccelerateRegion and IdleRegion->BrakeRegion use different route-token guards (4 vs 5), so I omit that candidate as satisfied/distinguishable. (6) NL3-DERIVED guard_disjointness (Accelerating->Cruising vs Accelerating->Braking) also uses distinct guards/tokens (6 for Reach_Speed vs 7/8 for Brake) so is omitted as distinguishable. I focus this lens's candidates on the structural default-entry gaps for the three regions, since these are the clearest source/model contrastive structural defects, keeping the outer Operate-level entry contract satisfied and unresolved-free. output.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner default-entry structure, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong local-exit targets by contrasting exact source-inventory obligations with the closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) the root/system->Operate initial-entry contract is satisfied by OffState->OperateState via 'start' and OperateState's own [*]->IdleRegion default entry, but each of the three regions inside OperateState (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) is itself a composite that owns a required default entry into its sole named operating leaf state (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState respectively per NL1/NL3 containment contracts), and none of those three regions has an initial edge targeting its named leaf state; each region's only initial pseudostate edge targets a synthetic 'UnspecifiedInitial' placeholder instead. This is a structural default-entry defect distinct from the already-satisfied outer Operate entry, so I derive three owner-scoped initial_entry contracts. (2) The AccelerateRegion's initial edge to CruisingState (transition:line:25) is conditional (guard R45RouteToken==6, no trigger), which the deterministic facts and verify_facts explicitly flag as INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted for initial-entry semantics; it cannot satisfy the region's default-entry obligation to AcceleratingState/CruisingState. (3) NL1-GROUP-DECL and NL3-GROUP-1 (Idle<->Accelerating/Cruising/Braking substate transitions) are represented in source only via region-to-region edges (IdleRegion->AccelerateRegion, etc.), never via edges naming the leaf states Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking directly; since those leaf states are unreachable from initial (per inspection/verify facts), the group-level transition endpoints are effectively wrong_target/unreachable relative to the named substates. (4) NL3-DERIVED event-consumer-coverage for 'stopping' is structurally consistent (Stop event has reachable consumers), so omitted. (5) The NL1-DERIVED guard_disjointness (Idle->Accelerating vs Idle->Braking) is not contrastively supported since IdleRegion->AccelerateRegion and IdleRegion->BrakeRegion use different route-token guards (4 vs 5), so I omit that candidate as satisfied/distinguishable. (6) NL3-DERIVED guard_disjointness (Accelerating->Cruising vs Accelerating->Braking) also uses distinct guards/tokens (6 for Reach_Speed vs 7/8 for Brake) so is omitted as distinguishable. I focus this lens's candidates on the structural default-entry gaps for the three regions, since these are the clearest source/model contrastive structural defects, keeping the outer Operate-level entry contract satisfied and unresolved-free. arguments.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner default-entry structure, transition-group guard collisions, and wrong local-exit targets by contrasting exact source-inventory obligations with the closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) the root/system->Operate initial-entry contract is satisfied by OffState->OperateState via 'start' and OperateState's own [*]->IdleRegion default entry, but each of the three regions inside OperateState (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) is itself a composite that owns a required default entry into its sole named operating leaf state (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState respectively per NL1/NL3 containment contracts), and none of those three regions has an initial edge targeting its named leaf state; each region's only initial pseudostate edge targets a synthetic 'UnspecifiedInitial' placeholder instead. This is a structural default-entry defect distinct from the already-satisfied outer Operate entry, so I derive three owner-scoped initial_entry contracts. (2) The AccelerateRegion's initial edge to CruisingState (transition:line:25) is conditional (guard R45RouteToken==6, no trigger), which the deterministic facts and verify_facts explicitly flag as INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL/refuted for initial-entry semantics; it cannot satisfy the region's default-entry obligation to AcceleratingState/CruisingState. (4) NL3-DERIVED event-consumer-coverage for 'stopping' is structurally consistent (Stop event has reachable consumers), so omitted. (5) The NL1-DERIVED guard_disjointness (Idle->Accelerating vs Idle->Braking) is not contrastively supported since IdleRegion->AccelerateRegion and IdleRegion->BrakeRegion use different route-token guards (4 vs 5), so I omit that candidate as satisfied/distinguishable. (6) NL3-DERIVED guard_disjointness (Accelerating->Cruising vs Accelerating->Braking) also uses distinct guards/tokens (6 for Reach_Speed vs 7/8 for Brake) so is omitted as distinguishable. I focus this lens's candidates on the structural default-entry gaps for the three regions, since these are the clearest source/model contrastive structural defects, keeping the outer Operate-level entry contract satisfied and unresolved-free. arguments.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, dead-end frontier facts, and termination stability, using the closed FCSTM inspection-equivalent/verify facts. The three regions each contain an authored leaf state (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState) that is structurally unreachable from initial because each region's own initial pseudostate targets an UnspecifiedInitial placeholder instead of the authored leaf, per inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics and verify_facts.non_proved reachability refutations. This directly affects the group-declared transition contracts (NL1-GROUP-DECL, NL3-GROUP-1) whose sources are Idle/Accelerating/Braking (the authored leaves) and the event-consumer-coverage derived contract (stopping event), since the only reachable consumer transitions are those attached to UnspecifiedInitial placeholders, not the authored leaf states. I also examine NL2 endpoints (start/keyOff) which are exactly satisfied structurally, and the NL1-INIT-1 owner entry to Operate/root which is exactly satisfied by OffState->OperateState arriving via start. No termination_state contract is supplied (Off/PoweredOff is not marked state_role=termination_state), so no termination candidate is derived. I derive one initial_entry-style structural observation is already covered by existing contracts (NL1-CONTAIN and GROUP contracts), so instead I focus on the reachable-consumer/dead-end consequences: the authored substates IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState are dead code with zero operational path, which undermines the transition-group contracts requiring transitions FROM those exact named substates, and undermines the stopping-event consumer-coverage contract because the reachable Braking->Idle transition is only realized via the UnspecifiedInitial placeholder, not the authored BrakingState, meaning the required substate-based transition never actually fires on the authored/reachable path.

decisions.reason: NL1 requires Idle as a concrete operating substate. The closed model shows IdleRegion's sole initial edge (transition:line:13) targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholder, not IdleState; inspection_equivalent_facts marks IdleState reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts refutes state:IdleState:line:11 reachability. The proposed rebuttal (placeholder functionally substitutes, or outer entry suffices) is a different, weaker property (outer composite entry) and does not rebut this owner-local default-entry requirement; it is defeated because the exact owner-local edge target is IdleState and the facts show it is not entered.

decisions.violated_obligation: IdleRegion's initial pseudostate edge must default-enter IdleState so the NL-required Idle substate is a live default target.

decisions.reason: NL1 lists 'Accelerating or Cruising' together with an explicit disjunction, unlike Idle/Braking which are singular required substates. The closed model shows AccelerateRegion's edges are transition:line:25 ([*]->CruisingState, guarded R45RouteToken==6, flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL and refuted for initial-entry semantics) and transition:line:26 ([*]->UnspecifiedInitial); the S2 receipt for [*]->AcceleratingState returns verdict=false and AcceleratingState is reachable_from_initial=false. Because NL1's own wording ties Accelerating and Cruising together disjunctively, a second competent reading -- that entering CruisingState default-satisfies the merged substate concept -- remains compatible with the same facts, even though the guard is separately flagged as diagnostically invalid for pure initial-entry semantics. This is a genuine undercutting alternative reading rather than a rebuttal that defeats the violation outright.
decisions.strongest_defeater: NL1's phrase 'Accelerating or Cruising' could be read as a single merged alternative-entry substate, so a guarded default entry into CruisingState (line 25) could be argued to satisfy that merged concept rather than requiring AcceleratingState specifically as the unconditional default target.
decisions.violated_obligation: AccelerateRegion's initial pseudostate must provide an unconditional default entry to AcceleratingState.
